overview.description: 41 Exchange is a trick-taking partnership game for four. Hearts permanent trump. 13 cards each; bid tricks (minimum 1-2); total bids must be at least 11 or redeal. Bids 1-6 score face value; 7+ score double. Fail bid = negative. Partnership wins when one partner reaches 41 points and the other has positive. Played in Middle East; related to 400 (Arba3meyeh).

history.origins: This trick-taking partnership game is often known as 400 (arba3meyeh). It is much played in Syria and to some extent in Lebanon. The name 400 has no clear explanation in the rules as that number does not arise in play. Considered a national game in the region.
timeline: Early 21st century: documented online as a popular Syrian partnership game, also played to some extent in Lebanon.
history.cultural: Much played in Syria and to some extent in Lebanon; considered a national game in the region.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack, ranking A-K-Q-J-10 down to 2; often French-made with French indices. Hearts are permanent trump.

rules.objective: Reach 41 points (one partner) with other partner positive.
rules.gameplay: Hearts trump. Bid tricks; sum of bids at least 11. Follow suit; trump or discard. 1-6 = face value; 7+ = double. Miss = negative.

strategy.intermediate: Count tricks; bid 7+ for double points but only when you can make it.
strategy.advanced: Partnership: signal through leads; defend by taking tricks when opponents overbid.
tips: Hearts always trump; bids must sum to at least 11.
One partner 41 and other positive wins.

list.name: Lebanese 400 scoring variation
list.description: Lebanese 400 follows the same core structure as 41 but uses a different minimum bid, higher mandatory minimum bids at certain score bands, and a non-linear trick-bid to points table.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Engine overrides for the Lebanese 400 scoring table are not yet modeled; only rules text describes the changes.

list.name: Higher target score and total-bid requirement
list.description: Some groups play to a target score of 44 instead of 41 and require the sum of all bids to reach at least 12 once players reach higher score bands, making games longer and riskier for leading partnerships.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Target score 44 and the higher total-bid requirement are described in rules text but have not yet been wired into structured engine override fields.

considerations: Hearts permanent trump; 13 each; bid tricks (sum 11+); 1-6 face value, 7+ double; fail negative. First to 41 with partner positive.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
